lines: Fourteen thousand years ago, people nursed a very sick puppy for weeks.
Its teeth tell the story.
So, did cavemen have pets?
Meet Moss. He wants a puppy.
Surprise one: in Germany, it was buried with a man and a woman.
It had a nasty illness called distemper.
Without care, it would die within three weeks.
But it lived about eight more weeks.
Experts think someone kept it warm, fed and clean.
A sick puppy can't work.
So it was probably loved.
Surprise two: dogs are our oldest animal friends.
They've lived with us at least fifteen thousand years.
Surprise three: a fox!
In Jordan, about sixteen thousand years ago, a fox was buried with a person.
A pet? Maybe. Scientists aren't sure.
Surprise four: in Israel, about twelve thousand years ago, a woman was buried with her hand on a puppy.
So yes, cavemen had furry friends.
Some were cared for like family.
And Moss? His puppy just stole his dinner.
